item.title: Trump’s war secretary Hegseth and Pacific Command chief Paparo may ‘soon visit China’
item.description: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and US Pacific Command head Admiral Samuel Paparo may visit China “soon”, according to a veteran China hand. Stephen Orlins, president of the non-profit organisation National Committee on United States-China Relations (NCUSCR), disclosed the potential visit during a video address at a conference on Friday in Sanya, in southern China’s Hainan province. item.title: China ‘Goddess of Mercy’ drone send-off reveals modern shift in funeral services
item.description: Videos showing a glowing Guanyin, or Goddess of Mercy, carried by a drone and another similar device disguised as a crane have attracted significant attention on Chinese social media. Together, the two devices recreate the traditional funeral send-off in which the deceased is said to “ascend to heaven.” In China, a common euphemism for someone who has died is that they have “ridden a crane to the Western Paradise,” or simply “gone west.” In the viral clips, released in early November, dozens of...

item.title: MTR Corporation orders halt to unauthorised work at station after column concerns
item.description: Hong Kong’s rail giant, the MTR Corporation, has ordered a contractor to fix substandard columns erected on the platform of a station under construction after discovering unauthorised remedial works to fill gaps of up to 30cm to the ceiling. The Highways Department said on Saturday that it had asked MTR Corp to submit a detailed investigation report within two weeks on the construction quality problem and the unauthorised remedial works at Tung Chung West station. item.title: US and China must join hands to measure rising AI tide
item.description: The next US-China talk on artificial intelligence should begin with a simple question: do the two governments actually understand how rapidly AI’s capabilities are improving? Before deciding what to do about the technology, Washington and Beijing need a common way to measure its progress. item.title: Why China is investing heavily in African push to bring mineral processing home
item.description: Chinese investors have backed mineral processing and manufacturing projects worth more than US$16 billion across Africa, a new report has concluded, amid an increasing push by countries to secure a greater share of the earnings from their natural resources.
